question: Does the HTTP fingerprint substrate discriminate same-status body-only drift where response status is identical (200 vs 200) but response bodies differ via server-side permission/content variation (Content-Length varies, body semantics differ), isolating body-only signal with status confound removed and yielding the complementary non-vacuous full > status test to the header-only success (full 1.0 > body/status 0.0, Content-Length isolation holds), plus writable permission-level and session-invalidation controls that produce discriminating positive (discrimination >=0.7) and valid null (FP<0.05) on localhost Flask HS256?
hypothesis: The HTTP fingerprint substrate hash(status_code || body_bytes || sorted_filtered_standard_headers) with EXCLUDED_HEADERS=[Date,Server,X-Request-Id] identical to parent EXP-RUNTIME-35741906498 will discriminate same-status body-only drift on localhost Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 + SQLite WAL (Werkzeug 3.1.8, Python 3.12.14): when the server returns identical 200 status codes but byte-different JSON bodies via a writable server-side state change (permission-filtered/content_variant), full-vector discrimination will be >0.5 (expected 1.0 deterministic) and B-BODY-ONLY >0.5, while B-STATUS-ONLY will be 0.0 (status confound removed), making full-vector strictly exceed status-only (full > status, non-vacuous complement to header-only's full 1.0 > body/status 0.0). Content-Length will vary proportionally to body length (verifying body semantics differ, not header-only), while non-Content-Length filtered headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Vary, Set-Cookie) remain identical, proving the signal is body-only not independent-header drift. The null same-state resampling will remain 0.0 (bootstrap CI contains 0.0, point estimate <=0.05). Separately, writable permission-level (reader vs admin body-filter, 200 vs 200) and classic writable controls permission-escalation (403 vs 200) and session-invalidation (401 vs 200) via SQLite role/session commits will each achieve discrimination >=0.7 with valid null FP<0.05, completing the localhost C-MEAS-VALID control matrix.
falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if, on verified same-status body-only drift comparisons where status is 200 vs 200 and bodies are byte-different via a committed server-side write (body SHA-256 differs, Content-Length differs, non-Content-Length filtered headers identical): (a) full-vector discrimination <=0.5, OR (b) B-BODY-ONLY <=0.5, OR (c) B-STATUS-ONLY !=0.0 (status confound not isolated), OR (d) full-vector fails to strictly exceed B-STATUS-ONLY (full <= status, equality at 1.0 is vacuous and fails by design as complement to header-only), OR (e) null control (same body state, two independent N=20 batches) discrimination >0.05 or 95% bootstrap CI does not contain 0.0, OR (f) Content-Length identical across states with different bodies or body SHA identical (no body variation), OR non-Content-Length filtered headers differ across body-only states (not body-only). Additionally, if writable permission-level body-filter (reader 200 vs admin 200) or classic writable controls (permission escalation 403 vs 200, session invalidation 401 vs 200) yield full discrimination <0.7 or their nulls >0.05, the matrix-completion claim is falsified for that control. Any single failure triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for the claimed condition. Infrastructure failure (server crash, SQLite commit not verified, non-200 where 200 required for body-only comparisons, body write not committed, fingerprint computation error) yields MEASUREMENT_INVALID, not falsification.

baselines.description: Fingerprint = status code only. Expected 0.0 on all same-status body-only drift comparisons (200 vs 200) and on body-only null. On classic permission-escalation (403 vs 200) and session-invalidation (401 vs 200) expected 1.0 (status discriminates). This is the strong null proving status confound isolated for body-only; if >0 on 200-vs-200 then experiment is not same-status.

Fingerprint = response body SHA-256 only (exact bytes). Expected >0.5 (ideally 1.0 deterministic) on all same-status body-only comparisons where bodies differ (A vs B/C, reader vs admin). Expected 0.0 on same-state null. Demonstrates body alone carries the discriminating signal when status is held constant. Content-Length variation corroborates body length difference.

Fingerprint = sorted filtered standard headers only (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary, Content-Type, Content-Length, Connection) excluding Date/Server/X-Request-Id. Expected >0 on body-only comparisons SOLELY via body-correlated Content-Length (body length differs); filtered headers excluding Content-Length expected 0.0 (B-HEADERS-NO-CLEN). This isolates independent header drift (should be 0) from body-correlated header change. Full-vector should track B-BODY-ONLY when status constant and Content-Length varies proportionally.

positive_control: Same-status body-only drift via writable server-side permission/content variation on localhost Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 + SQLite WAL (or in-memory dict with WAL COMMIT semantics). Server exposes POST /admin/set_body_variant (or POST /admin/set_permission with content_variant column) which updates SQLite table body_config/content_variant and commits before 200 response; verified by SELECT before observation. Three body states on GET /resource (authenticated with valid JWT, status 200 for all): STATE_A baseline body {"data":"hello","version":1} 31 bytes SHA d0ca833f843c6d70ec9d6755f52a92dcbfc8b4ab601b871bced09ad027172e34, STATE_B reader-filtered body {"data":"hello","version":1,"role":"reader","items":["a","b"]} ~52 bytes SHA distinct, STATE_C admin body {"data":"hello","version":1,"role":"admin","items":["a","b","c"],"admin_note":"sensitive:42","count":42} ~95 bytes SHA distinct. Non-Content-Length headers held constant across A/B/C: Cache-Control max-age=3600, ETag W/"fixed-aaa-111", Vary Accept-Encoding, no Set-Cookie (verified raw). Content-Length must vary (31 vs 52 vs 95) proving body semantics differ. Primary comparison A vs C (max body distance) must achieve full >0.5 and body-only >0.5 with status-only 0.0 and full > status strictly. Per-body isolations A vs B and A vs C each tested; at least 2/2 must show body-only >0.5. Additional writable controls in same server lifecycle: (P1) permission-filtered body via role lookup (reader token vs admin token) 200 vs 200 same as above, discrimination >=0.7; (P2) classic permission escalation via UPDATE users SET role (or body_config) causing GET /resource 403 vs 200 with different body, discrimination >=0.7; (S) session invalidation via DELETE sessions causing GET /resource 401 vs 200, discrimination >=0.7. Each control verified by SQLite SELECT commit before batch. Full-vector and body-only must each be >=0.7 on P2/S; status-only must be 1.0 on P2/S (status differs) but 0.0 on body-only A vs C. Setup verified by: (1) SQLite body_config committed before observation batch (SELECT); (2) status 200 on all body-only observations (any non-200 fails validity for that comparison); (3) body SHA-256 inequality across A vs C and equality within null resamples; (4) raw non-CLEN headers identical across A/B/C (logged).
null_control: Same-state resampling (body stability) plus classic nulls: (N1) two independent batches of N=20 GET /resource from the same body state STATE_A (no server write between batches, jitter 50-150ms, SEED=44), expected full-vector discrimination =0.0 (both batches produce identical fingerprints; all 20 fingerprints within each batch byte-identical, set size 1), bootstrap 95% CI must contain 0.0 with point estimate <=0.05 (FP<0.05), and B-STATUS-ONLY=0.0 and B-BODY-ONLY=0.0 on null; (N2) same for STATE_C (admin body) resampled as exploratory, expected 0.0; (N3) permission/session stable nulls: same-state 403 resampled and same-state 401 resampled each 0.0 to verify false-positive <0.05 on status-varying controls. This tests false-positive rate when bodies/headers/status stable — complements parent's header-stability null. Degenerate CI [0.0,0.0] is EXPECTED deterministic and declared valid when set sizes are 1.
measurement_validity: Server state snapshot: body_config/content_variant or permission role read from SQLite and logged before each observation batch; POST /admin/set_body_variant commit verified by subsequent SELECT; header_config held constant and logged before each body-only batch to confirm no independent header drift

Status identity verified for body-only comparisons: all observations in A vs B vs C must be status=200; any non-200 aborts that comparison as measurement failure (MEASUREMENT_INVALID) except for classic P2/S controls where 403/401 is expected and verified separately

Body byte-difference verified: SHA-256(body_bytes) must be distinct across STATE_A vs STATE_C (and A vs B) and Content-Length must differ proportionally (body_len 31 vs 52 vs 95); SHA-256 equality within null resamples verified; Content-Length header value must equal body_len (proving no truncation). Non-Content-Length filtered headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Vary, Set-Cookie) must be identical across A/B/C (proving body-only not header-confounded); Date, Server, X-Request-Id excluded and logged

Header inclusion/exclusion: Date, Server, X-Request-Id excluded from fingerprint exactly as parent (EXCLUDED_HEADERS same set); Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary INCLUDED but held constant across body-only states; any unexpected variation in non-CLEN headers is validity failure. B-HEADERS-ONLY computed with same algorithm; B-HEADERS-NO-CLEN (filtered headers minus Content-Length) also computed to prove zero independent header signal

Fingerprint computation: hash(status || body_bytes || sorted_filtered_headers) identical algorithm to parent (research/experiments/EXP-RUNTIME-35697043449/run_experiment.py:compute_fingerprint and EXP-RUNTIME-35741906498/run_experiment.py); code path hashed and stored in provenance; recomputation by auditor must match within 0 mismatches

Seed and jitter: SEED=44 deterministic, jitter 50-150ms uniform between observations same as parent for reproducibility; N=20 per state nominal (7 batches x20 =140 raw lines expected: A/B/C 60 + N1/N2 40 + P2 20 + S 20), effective distinct N=1 reported alongside nominal N=20; degenerate CI disclosure required

Degenerate CI disclosure: with deterministic responses fingerprints within a state are byte-identical (expected set size 1 per state); bootstrap CI will be degenerate [1.0,1.0] or [0.0,0.0] and is reported as deterministic, not as inferential precision; effective distinct N=1 reported; jitter had no observable effect on deterministic body/header fingerprints

Server freshness: Flask dev server started fresh per run on 127.0.0.1 with free port (discoverable, default 19849 or next free), no residual body_config/header_config; port and Flask/PyJWT/SQLite/Werkzeug versions recorded in provenance; server killed on exit; SQLite WAL COMMIT verified before each batch via batch_state_log

Timing: body_config write committed (SQLite WAL COMMIT or dict update) before next observation batch; sequential request-response, no concurrent load (concurrency explicitly out of scope and listed in unresolved); inter-batch delay 100ms to ensure commit visibility

Artifact integrity: run_experiment.py, raw_observations.jsonl, experiment_result.json SHA-256 logged in provenance; recomputation of Jaccard distances by auditor must match producer; batch_state_log.jsonl records committed body SHA, Content-Length, header_config per batch for audit verification
product_consequence_positive: C-MEAS-VALID advances within EXPERIMENTAL with ceiling expanded to include same-status body-only drift — the complementary half of the localhost discrimination matrix to header-only (EXP-RUNTIME-35741906498). Full 1.0 > status 0.0 with body-only 1.0 demonstrates the substrate detects server-side permission/content variation when bodies differ but status identical (Content-Length varies, non-CLEN headers identical), proving body signal isolated from status confound. Combined with header-only 1.0 > body/status 0.0 and permission 403-vs-200/session 401-vs-200 >=0.7 and nulls <0.05, the full localhost matrix (header-only, body-only, status-varying maximally-distinct, null stability) is complete for Flask dev server HS256. This unblocks C-FRESHNESS (detect content change without status change) and C-DELTA-REPAIR (local body perturbation measurement) for localhost synthetic testing with both header-only and body-only branches validated. Does NOT promote to VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE: still bounded to Flask dev server localhost single client sequential, no production WSGI (gunicorn)/nginx/CDN/load-balancer, no concurrency/HTTP2/TLS, no distributed session replication, degenerate CI effective N=1, jitter no effect, body/header value magnitudes limited to 3 variants.
product_consequence_negative: C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL with same-status body-only drift falsified: HTTP fingerprint substrate (status+body+filtered headers) cannot discriminate server-side body-only state changes when status is held constant at 200, or can only do so below 0.5 / with status leakage / with independent header confound, or null false-positives, or Content-Length not varying. This means current body hashing / Content-Length handling / Flask dev body handling is insufficient for same-status content drift detection, despite header-only success. C-FRESHNESS cases where response bodies vary due to permission/content filtering (200 vs 200 with different JSON) and C-DELTA-REPAIR cases where local content perturbation keeps status 200 remain unmeasurable with this substrate; alternative substrates (response-body-aware DOM, explicit body-diff, production middleware body handling) or body-value magnitude changes are required. The complementary non-vacuous full>status test remains unproven, so the matrix stays half-closed and distributed/production body-drift testing is not yet valid. Negative result is still high-information: it bounds the substrate to header-only + status-varying conditions and prevents false trust in body-only freshness guards.
estimated_cost: Low: single Flask dev server + SQLite WAL on localhost, no external dependencies beyond Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT (already installed), 7 batches x20 =140 GET observations plus setup writes, ~6-8 min execution, deterministic; no Docker, no nginx, no CDN, no distributed nodes; same cost class as parent header-only (EXP-RUNTIME-35741906498).
expected_information_gain: High and discriminating: completes the other half of the vacuous-C4 fix. Header-only just proved full 1.0 > body/status 0.0 with Content-Length isolation; this is the complementary non-vacuous full 1.0 > status 0.0 where body is the sole varying signal (Content-Length varies). Positive outcome closes the localhost C-MEAS-VALID control matrix needed for all freshness/delta-repair claims (both metadata-only and content-only drift measurable). Negative outcome is equally decisive: it falsifies body-only detection with current fingerprint and forces substrate redesign (body hashing, Content-Length inclusion, or Flask dev body handling) before any production or distributed testing. Either outcome resolves parent handoff unresolved[3] and directly determines whether freshness/delta experiments can trust body-only server-state changes on localhost before scaling.
